questions.question: Write a design brief for the model rescue device and explain what each sentence contributes.
questions.expected_answer: Example: Emergency workers need a tool to prise open crushed vehicle doors and free trapped people. I am going to design and make a working model of a hydraulic rescue device for the Technology class. It will use water-filled syringes to drive a pair of linked-lever jaws that open and close, demonstrating how hydraulics and levers combine to produce a large controlled force. It will be made from the cardboard, syringes and tubing provided and finished in two weeks. The first sentence states the problem and the people affected, the second the product and its user, the third the function and purpose, and the fourth the main limits.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a specification and a constraint, and give two examples of each for the rescue device.
questions.expected_answer: A specification describes a feature or performance the product must have and should be testable, for example the jaws must open at least 40 millimetres, or the jaws must hold a 50 gram block without slipping. A constraint describes a limit on the project within which the designer must work, for example only the cardboard, syringes and tubing provided may be used, or the device must fit on an A4 sheet and be finished in two making lessons.

questions.question: Describe how you would move from the brief to a chosen design and a materials list.
questions.expected_answer: Sketch at least two or three initial ideas that work in genuinely different ways, labelled with a few words on how each works. Draw up a table with the ideas across the top and the specifications and constraints down the side, score each cell with a tick, cross or question mark, choose the idea with the best score and write the reasons, borrowing a good feature from a rejected idea if useful. Then list a material for each part with a reason tied to a specification, such as two layers of card for the arms because one layer bends, split pins for pivots because they allow turning, and a larger syringe at the jaws to multiply the push.
